The IVOA-defined obscore table, containing generic metadata for datasets within this datacenter.

 SELECT dataproduct_type, s_ra, s_dec, access_url FROM ivoa.obscore WHERE contains(point('ICRS', 144.7989,30.6), s_region) = 1 AND em_min < 0.000006231 AND em_max > 0.000006231
Table that contains information about the filters.

Table that contains the main information and properties of the coadded images. These images have been created combining the individual processed science images for each filter. The detection and the object properties contained in the other tables have been computed from these images.
Table that contains the main information and properties of the reduced individual images. These images are the ones used to create the coadded images (TileImage table).
Table that contains all the calibration data of the tiles. For each tile, this table contains the zero point and error obtained using different calibration methods.

Table that contains the main parameters of the astronomical objects detected in the images. The object detection is performed independently on each filter using SExtractor. Flux data is adjusted by the image Zero Point and is in 10<sup>-30</sup>erg/s/cm<sup>2</sup>/Hz units.

Table that contains the main parameters of the astronomical duplicated objects detected in the images. The sources listed in this table have been considered duplicated detections as they are at the same location of another detection in an adjacent image that has better data quality. Only the counterpart with lower quality is listed in this table. Flux data is adjusted by the image Zero Point and is in 10<sup>30</sup>erg/s/cm<sup>2</sup>/Hz units.

Table that contains the main parameters of the astronomical objects detected in the images. The object detection and aperture definition is performed in a reference band ('rSDSS') and the measurements are done in each filter using SExtractor (Dual Mode). Array columns (type[]) contains measures for each filter (NULL if the image in the filter is not available). Enumeration 'jplus' can be used to refer filter positions in the array. Flux data is adjusted by the image Zero Point and is in 10<sup>-30</sup>erg/s/cm<sup>2</sup>/Hz units.

Table that contains the photometric redshifts of the astronomical objects. The photometric redshifts have been obtained using the Lephare package. The photometric information in table FNuDualObj has been used as input.

Table that contains the B-V color excess due to Milky Way dust at the position of the sources. The integrated E(B-V), this is, estimated at infinity, is provided and was estimated from the Schlafly & Finkbeiner (2011) recalibration of the Schlegel, Finkbeiner & Davis (1998) infrared-based (COBE/DIRBE and IRAS/ISSA) dust map. Objects are identified by tile_id and number columns. The E(B-V) is computed for those objects in dual mode tables.

Table that contains star galaxy classification of the objects detected in dual mode. Objects are identified by tile_id and number columns and the classification corresponds to those objects contained in dual mode tables (FLambdaDualObj, FNuDualObj or MagABDualObj) and dual mode duplicated objects tables (DuplicatedFLambdaDualObj, DuplicatedFNuDualObj or DuplicatedMagABDualObj).

This table contains the outcome of applying BANNJOS (del Pino et al. 2024, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...691A.221D/abstract), a machine learning pipeline that uses Bayesian neural networks to provide the probability distribution function (PDF) of the star/QSO/galaxy classification, when applied to J-PLUS DR3 sources. The source code can be found here or here.

Selection of the most relevant columns of each classifier: SExtractor's CLASS_STAR, the star/galaxy classification (López-Sanjuan et al. 2019b) from StarGalClass table, and the BANNJOS artificial neural networks based star/QSO/galaxy classification (del Pino et al. 2024) from ClassBANNJOS table.

J-HERTz (J-PLUS Heritage Exploration of Radio Targets) is a value-added catalog that combines optical photometry from J-PLUS DR3 with low-frequency radio data from the LOFAR Two-Metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) DR2. The catalog includes stars, galaxies and QSOs up to z < 5. It is aimed at studying radio emission, AGN activity, and galaxy evolution. This is a reduced version with value-added and derived parameters. The paper describing the complete catalog is: Fernández Gil et al. 2026 (https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-4365/ae2016).
